1: AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE PLANNING AND ZONING ORDINANCE OF THE TOWN OF CLERMONT, GEORGIA, BEING DESIGNATED AS ORDINANCE NO. 97-01, WHICH WAS DULY PASSED ON MARCH 4, 1997; TO STRIKE IN ITS ENTIRETY,
2: APPLICATION FEES; AND SUBSTITUTE IN LIEU THEREOF NEW SECTIONS 6-1, 6-2, AND 6-3 GOVERNING LANDUSE APPLICATION FEES; TO REPEAL CONFLICTING PROVISIONS OF OTHER TOWN ORDINANCES; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
3: The purpose of this Article is to set fees which shall be required in order to enforce the provisions of this Landuse Ordinance for the Town of Clermont.
4:
A. Fees for the Administration of the Landuse Regulations as set by Sub-sections E and F (or as hereinafter set by Resolution by the Town Council), shall be collected previous to action by any Committee, Board, or the Town Council or final action by any Administrative Officer. An application shall not be considered complete until the fee is paid.

B. No Committee, Board or Administrative Officer shall waive payment of the required fee except that an amendment to the Landuse Ordinance proposed by the Town Council shall not be assessed a fee. Should the Board of Appeals find in favor of the appellant on an action of alleged error of an Administrative Official, the assessed fee shall be refunded.

C. A building permit will be issued, however, NO CONSTRUCTION on any property can begin without the submittal of : (1) a plat showing all lot lines, setbacks, position of the proposed building in relation to the lot lines and setbacks; (2) a copy of the deed on the property; (3) copy of the septic system permit issued by the Hall County Health Department; (4) copy of driveway permit from the Department of Transportation (only if driveway is off of a state road). When a building permit is sought and the lot, tract, or parcel of land contains more than the required acreage required by this Ordinance for the Use applied for, the required lot or acreage must be

shown, separately from the remainder of the lot, tract, or parcel of land, on a survey prepared by a competent, licensed surveyor, and said survey must be submitted for Town Council approval. Upon approval by the Town Council, said required lot or acreage shall be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court of Hall County. The Town Council shall not have any power to prohibit the enforcement of these provisions for any reason. All construction must receive a permit before any construction begins.

D. Definitions:

Conditional Use: A use which would not be appropriate without restriction throughout a zoning district and is not automatically permitted by right within a zoning district, but which may be permitted within a zoning district subject to meeting specific conditions (such as controls on number, size, area, location and activities) contained in these regulations or required by the Governing Body. Such uses may be permitted only if approved by the Governing Body in accordance with the regulations established herein.

Manufactured Home: A structure, built to conform to National Standards embodied in the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974 as amended, 42 U.S.C. 5401, et seq. administered by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), transportable in one or more sections, which in the traveling mode, is eight (8) body feet or more in width or more than forty (40) body feet in length, or when erected on site, is three hundred twenty (320) or more square feet, and which is built on a permanent foundations when connected to the required utilities, and includes mandatory plumbing, heating, air-conditioning and electrical systems contained therein. A manufactured home displays a certificate from the U.S. Department of Housing & Urban Development.

Mobile Home: A structure, transportable in one or more sections, which in the traveling mode, is eight (8) body feet or more in width or forty (40) body feet or more in length, or when erected on site, is three hundred twenty (320) or more square feet and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without permanent foundation when connected to required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning and electrical systems contained therein. Must be seven (7) years old or less to be located in the Town Limits of Clermont.

G. Authorization to change and set the amount of fees for the Administration of the Land Use Regulations by Resolution of the Town Council.

The purpose behind requiring regulatory fees for the administration of the land use regulations is to offset as much as possible the costs and expenses of the Town of Clermont in the administration of its land use regulations. As provided by the land use regulations, all property owners within the Town of Clermont derive a benefit from the land use regulations and the provision of these services by the Town of Clermont. In order to hold down any loss to the Town of Clermont due to the provision of this service and the administrative cost incurred by the Town

in the administration of this service, the Town Council is hereby authorized, as determined in its discretion to cover the regulatory cost and expenses of administering this ordinance, to modify and change the amount of the fees for the administration of these land use regulations, by resolution duly passed in a public meeting of the Town Council, in order to have an efficient modification of the amount of the fees. Any new fees set by the Town Council by proper resolution shall be available for review by any person pursuant to the Open Records Act, and shall be posted for at least one (1) week after passage of the resolution upon the public bulletin board at the Town Hall. The Town Council further finds that the amount of the regulatory fees charged by the Town to defray its costs is no an amendment to the text of the zoning ordinance, as defined by 0.C.G.A. § 36-66-3(4)(B) in that the amount of the regulatory fees does not affect or change the uses of property subject to the zoning ordinance.
